latest_interestingness_rationale: Natural extension of the RAAG coarse-separation characterization to graph products of virtually nilpotent groups; meaningful within geometric group theory with clear structural consequences, but specialised in scope.
latest_viability_rationale: Natural generalisation of proven RAAG result but depends on extending relatively hyperbolic/ thickness tools; plausible but requires nontrivial technical work.
latest_label_rationale: The authors pose this generalization to graph products as a conjecture; they prove the RAAG case but do not prove this broader statement here.
latest_evidence_snippet: "On the one hand, we expect that: Let Γ be a finite graph and G a collection... The graph product ΓG is coarsely separable..." (lines 236–240).

title: Coloopless and cosimple zonotopes, and the Lonely Runner Conjectures
latest_label_rationale: The statement includes both the classical LRC and the shifted sLRC; the paper reports explicit counterexamples to the shifted version, so the combined conjectural statement as written is false.
latest_evidence_snippet: "We show explicit counterexamples to both the shifted Lonely Runner Conjecture (starting at n=5) ..." and the conjecture statement (lines 242–245,259–261).

title: Anti-concentration of polynomials: $L^{p}$ balls and symmetric measures
latest_interestingness_rationale: A uniform, dimension-free variance lower bound for degree-d homogeneous polynomials under all isotropic log-concave H_n-invariant measures would yield strong anti-concentration consequences; proven for d≤3, even-degree complexities make it challenging but central.
latest_viability_rationale: Proved for d=2,3 and method extends partially; even-degree classification (d>=4) poses hard obstacles (many convex polynomials, NP-hard checks), so resolution within five years plausible but uncertain.
latest_label_rationale: The paper states the L^2 lower-bound conjecture explicitly and notes they could not establish it uniformly (only d=2,3 cases treated); it is presented as an open question.
latest_evidence_snippet: Lines 447–456, 463–466: authors state Conjecture \ref{conj:l2bound} and remark they could not establish it uniformly, giving computed C_2,C_3 and partial results.

title: Anti-concentration of polynomials: $L^{p}$ balls and symmetric measures
latest_interestingness_rationale: Connects improved small-ball exponents (α>1/d) to matching Fourier decay for polynomials under log-concave measures. Useful bridge between probabilistic and harmonic estimates, technically plausible but conditional and partially known in special cases.
latest_viability_rationale: Known in product/independence cases and heuristics connect small-ball to Fourier decay; attainable with technical advances, but requires new uniform analytic tools beyond current partial results.
latest_label_rationale: The Fourier-decay implication from improved small-ball exponent is posed as Conjecture \ref{conj:expo} and is not proved in the paper; authors raise it as an open question.
latest_evidence_snippet: Lines 490–495 and 483–488: Conjecture \ref{conj:expo} is stated and authors discuss related partial results but do not prove the general implication.

title: Limit Values of Character Sums in Frobenius Formula of Three Permutations
body_tex: If the triple of conjugacy classes \(C_1, C_2, C_3\) of the symmetric group ${\frak S}_n$ are all 3-derangements, then the branching data \(C_1,C_2,C_3\) is realizable.
plain_text: If the triple of conjugacy classes \(C_1, C_2, C_3\) of the symmetric group $ S _n$ are all 3-derangements, then the branching data \(C_1,C_2,C_3\) is realizable.
latest_interestingness_rationale: A natural Hurwitz-type realizability conjecture for symmetric-group triples avoiding 1,2,3-cycles; interesting within branched-cover/Hurwitz problems but narrow compared to field-wide conjectures.
latest_viability_rationale: Hurwitz realizability for 3-derangement triples has strong computational evidence and no counterexamples; group-theoretic techniques may settle it in the near term.
latest_label_rationale: Proposed by the authors as a new conjecture on realizability of branching data when all classes are 3-derangements; presented as open and motivated by absence of counterexamples.
latest_evidence_snippet: Lines 1416–1420: "...for all the known unrealisable branching data, no case ... contains any 1,2, or 3-cycles. This leads us to the following conjecture: If the triple ... are all 3-derangements, then the branching data ... is realizable."

title: Cartier integration of infinitesimal 2-braidings via 2-holonomy of the CMKZ 2-connection, II: The pentagonator
latest_interestingness_rationale: Acyclicity of the Drinfeld–Kohno 2-algebra would have strong structural consequences in categorified braid/quantum algebra theory and simplify construction of braided monoidal 2-categories.
latest_viability_rationale: Acyclicity of the Drinfeld-Kohno 2-algebra is a foundational higher-algebra conjecture; low-n cases seem clear but full generality appears challenging within five years.
latest_label_rationale: Authors state this as their 'fundamental conjecture' about acyclicity of the Drinfeld-Kohno 2-algebra; it is posed and used as an open hypothesis, not proved.
latest_evidence_snippet: Lines 783–786: "We are now ready to state our fundamental conjecture ... Conjecture: For n in N, the n-th Drinfeld-Kohno 2-algebra is acyclic, i.e. ker(∂)=0."

title: Hyper-K\"ahler varieties: Lagrangian fibrations, atomic sheaves, and categories
latest_interestingness_rationale: Central expectation in symplectic/irreducible symplectic variety theory; finiteness of pi1(M_reg) impacts quasi-étale covers and classification of singular hyper-Kähler varieties.
latest_viability_rationale: Deep structural conjecture in irreducible symplectic varieties tied to Lagrangian fibration conjectures; nontrivial and plausibly resists resolution within five years.
latest_label_rationale: Stated as a general expectation (Rapagnetta) and referenced as an open conjecture; authors do not claim a proof and discuss implications if true.
latest_evidence_snippet: Lines 480–485: "We mention the following general expectation, which we learned from Rapagnetta... Let M be a projective irreducible symplectic variety. Then M_reg has finite fundamental group."

title: Hyper-K\"ahler varieties: Lagrangian fibrations, atomic sheaves, and categories
latest_interestingness_rationale: The SYZ/semiampleness conjecture is a core open problem in hyper-Kähler geometry, directly producing Lagrangian fibrations and connecting to abundance-type statements with wide structural consequences.
latest_viability_rationale: The SYZ/abundance-type conjecture for primitive symplectic varieties is a major open problem; despite progress on examples, a general proof seems unlikely in five years.
latest_label_rationale: The SYZ conjecture is explicitly described as 'the main open problem' and presented without proof; known to hold for known examples but remains conjectural.
latest_evidence_snippet: Lines 873–880: "The main open problem ... is the so called SYZ Conjecture... Let M be a projective primitive symplectic variety and let L be a nef line bundle on M. Then L is semiample."

title: Hyper-K\"ahler varieties: Lagrangian fibrations, atomic sheaves, and categories
latest_interestingness_rationale: A focused derived-category/atomic-object conjecture linking simplicity to 1-obstructedness; important for deformation theory of objects but specialized to categorical/hyper-Kähler contexts.
latest_viability_rationale: Beckmann's equivalence between atomicity and 1-obstructedness is a concrete categorical statement; active research and structural theorems make near-term resolution plausible but nontrivial.
latest_label_rationale: Attributed to Beckmann as a conjecture (Conjecture A & corollary), stated explicitly and not proved here; authors reference it as open.
latest_evidence_snippet: Lines 1352–1357: "Beckmann conjectures ... For simple atomic objects the reverse implication also holds. Conjecture (Beckmann): Let E in D^b(X) be a simple atomic object. Then E is 1-obstructed."

title: Hyper-K\"ahler varieties: Lagrangian fibrations, atomic sheaves, and categories
latest_interestingness_rationale: Technical but meaningful for constructing symplectic moduli spaces: asserts hard Lefschetz for obstruction-image elements, primarily influential within moduli and atomic-sheaf theory.
latest_viability_rationale: Hard Lefschetz property for obstruction-image elements is technical and tied to moduli smoothness; approachable but depends on deeper atomic/obstruction results.
latest_label_rationale: Stated as Beckmann's conjecture in the text; presented as an open statement necessary for symplectic moduli constructions and not proved in the paper.
latest_evidence_snippet: Lines 1634–1638: "To have a symplectic moduli space one should prove the following conjecture, which was put forward in [Beckmann]. Conjecture: Let E be a stable atomic sheaf, then any nonzero element ... has the hard Lefschetz property."

title: Hyper-K\"ahler varieties: Lagrangian fibrations, atomic sheaves, and categories
latest_interestingness_rationale: A concrete structural claim (skew-symmetry of Yoneda product) for stable atomic bundles on hyper-Kähler manifolds; useful for smoothness arguments but fairly specialized.
latest_viability_rationale: Skew-symmetry of the Yoneda product for stable atomic bundles is a difficult formality-type claim; progress likely requires new structural inputs—moderate-low near-term chance.
latest_label_rationale: Explicitly presented as Beckmann's conjecture (difficult conjecture) needed for smoothness arguments; the paper does not prove it.
latest_evidence_snippet: Lines 1673–1681: "The proof will be drastically simplified if one could establish the following difficult conjecture ... Conjecture (Beckmann): Let E be a stable atomic vector bundle on a hyper-Kähler manifold. Then the Yoneda product ... is skew-symmetric."

title: Extending partial edge-colorings of bounded size in Cartesian products of graphs
body_tex:
\label{basic} \cite{cartesian}
    If $G$ is a graph that every precoloring of at most $k < \chi'(G)$ edges can be extended to a proper $\chi'(G)$-edge-coloring, then every precoloring of at most $k+1$ edges of $G \square K_2$ is extendable to a proper $(\chi'(G)+1)$-edge-coloring of $G \square K_2$.
plain_text: If $G$ is a graph that every precoloring of at most $k < '(G)$ edges can be extended to a proper $'(G)$-edge-coloring, then every precoloring of at most $k+1$ edges of $G K_2$ is extendable to a proper $('(G)+1)$-edge-coloring of $G K_2$.
latest_interestingness_rationale: Casselgren's conjecture for Cartesian product with K2 generalizes hypercube extension results; a meaningful problem in edge-precoloring extension theory with solid combinatorial content but limited cross-field breadth.
latest_viability_rationale: Paper settles numerous cases (trees, complete, complete bipartite, small Δ, triangle-free r-regular with k<Δ, subcubic Class 2). Remaining general higher-Δ/Class 2 cases look technical but plausibly resolvable within five years.
latest_label_rationale: The Casselgren–Petros–Fufa basic conjecture is cited as motivation; the paper verifies many special cases but does not prove the conjecture in full generality.
latest_evidence_snippet: Conjecture: If G has the extension property up to k<χ'(G), then every precoloring of at most k+1 edges of G□K_2 is extendable. Paper verifies trees, complete graphs, small Δ, and other special cases, but not the full conjecture.

title: Extending partial edge-colorings of bounded size in Cartesian products of graphs
body_tex:
\label{general}
    If $G$ is a graph that every precoloring of at most $k < \chi'(G)$ edges can be extended to a proper $\chi'(G)$-edge-coloring and $H$ is a graph that every precoloring of at most $l < \chi'(H)$ edges can be extended to a proper $\chi'(H)$-edge-coloring, then every precoloring of at most $k+l+1$ edges of $G \square H$ is extendable to a proper $(\chi'(G)+\chi'(H))$-edge-coloring of $G \square H$.
plain_text: If $G$ is a graph that every precoloring of at most $k < '(G)$ edges can be extended to a proper $'(G)$-edge-coloring and $H$ is a graph that every precoloring of at most $l < '(H)$ edges can be extended to a proper $'(H)$-edge-coloring, then every precoloring of at most $k+l+1$ edges of $G H$ is extendable to a proper $('(G)+'(H))$-edge-coloring of $G H$.
latest_interestingness_rationale: A broad generalization to arbitrary Cartesian products (G square H) that, if true, would resolve many extension questions; important within graph edge-coloring though specialized to this subfield.
latest_viability_rationale: Significant partial progress for many graph classes (trees, even cycles, triangle-free r-regular, subcubic G with K2), but the general broad statement likely needs new techniques—moderate chance of resolution in five years.
latest_label_rationale: The generalized Cartesian-product conjecture is proposed; the authors prove it in various restricted settings but do not claim a complete proof.
latest_evidence_snippet: Conjecture (general): If G and H have extension properties up to k,l then any precoloring of at most k+l+1 edges of G□H is extendable. Stated as open; paper proves special cases only.

title: Extending partial edge-colorings of bounded size in Cartesian products of graphs
body_tex: Let $G$ be an $r$-regular, triangle-free graph. If any precoloring of at most $k < r$ edges of $G$ can be extended to a proper $\chi'(G)$-edge-coloring of $G$, then any precoloring of at most $k+n$ edges of $G \square K_{n,n}$ can be extended to a proper $(\chi'(G)+n)$-edge-coloring of $G \square K_{n,n}$.
plain_text: Let $G$ be an $r$-regular, triangle-free graph. If any precoloring of at most $k < r$ edges of $G$ can be extended to a proper $'(G)$-edge-coloring of $G$, then any precoloring of at most $k+n$ edges of $G K_ n,n $ can be extended to a proper $('(G)+n)$-edge-coloring of $G K_ n,n $.
latest_interestingness_rationale: A specific extension statement for r-regular triangle-free G and K_{n,n} linking to hypercube conjectures; interesting for implications but conditional and focused.
latest_viability_rationale: Substantial partial results (many H, subcubic cases) indicate active progress, but essential triangle-free/regular assumptions and new techniques are required to handle K_{n,n}; plausible within 5 years but uncertain.
latest_label_rationale: This K_{n,n}-variant is posed in concluding remarks as an open conjecture; the paper does not resolve it and suggests it would imply other open conjectures.
latest_evidence_snippet: Concluding remarks: Conjecture: For r-regular triangle-free G, if precolorings of ≤k<r edges extend, then any precoloring of ≤k+n edges of G□K_{n,n} extends. Authors leave this as open, noting implications.

title: Extending partial edge-colorings of bounded size in Cartesian products of graphs
body_tex:
\cite{hypercube}
    If $n$ and $d$ are positive integers, and $\varphi$ is a proper edge-precoloring of $K_{n,n}^d$, with at most $nd - 1$ precolored edges, then $\varphi$ extends to a proper $nd$-edge-coloring of $K_{n,n}^d$.
plain_text: If $n$ and $d$ are positive integers, and $$ is a proper edge-precoloring of $K_ n,n ^d$, with at most $nd - 1$ precolored edges, then $$ extends to a proper $nd$-edge-coloring of $K_ n,n ^d$.
latest_interestingness_rationale: Nontrivial edge-precoloring extension problem for Cartesian products/hypercube powers: meaningful within graph-coloring theory with structural consequences for hypercube cases, but limited broader mathematical reach.
latest_viability_rationale: Specialized graph-coloring conjecture with partial progress in Cartesian products; active area but still requires new ideas to remove structural assumptions—moderate near-term chance.
latest_label_rationale: Presented as a cited conjecture of Casselgren, Markström and Pham and not proved in this paper; authors state it would follow from their broader conjecture but do not resolve it.
latest_evidence_snippet: Lines 722–726: "Establishing this conjecture ... would imply a solution to the following conjecture of Casselgren, Markström and Pham. ... If n and d are positive integers ... with at most nd-1 precolored edges, then φ extends ..."

title: The Separating Noether Number of Finite Abelian Groups
latest_label_rationale: The paper proves the conjectured support conclusion for all finite abelian groups of rank ≥2 as an application of its main theorem, thus resolving the conjecture in the intended range.
latest_evidence_snippet: As an application, we prove that ... the conjectured support conclusion of Schefler, Zhao, and Zhong holds for all finite abelian groups of rank at least 2. (Conjecture 5.4 from SZZ is stated earlier.)

title: Linear spaces in Hessian loci of cubic hypersurfaces
latest_interestingness_rationale: The Ciliberto–Ottaviani conjecture on birationality of the Hessian map is a central, longstanding problem in projective algebraic geometry with notable consequences for reconstruction and moduli questions.
latest_viability_rationale: Generically finite and proved in key cases (cubic surfaces, Waring-rank loci); recent progress on cubic threefolds gives evidence, but full uniform birationality across all d,n is broad and likely not resolved imminently.
latest_label_rationale: This is the Ciliberto–Ottaviani conjecture stated here; the paper proves special cases (evidence for cubic threefolds) but does not claim the full conjecture is resolved.
latest_evidence_snippet: Conjecture (Ciliberto-Ottaviani): The hessian map h_{d,n} is birational onto its image for every d≥3, n≥2, except (d,n)=(3,2). Authors note prior partial results and give evidence in special cubic cases but do not prove the full conjecture.

title: Simplex Stratification and Phase Boundaries in the Partition Graph
latest_interestingness_rationale: Triangular-number threshold for first appearance of simplex layers in the partition graph is an elegant combinatorial pattern suggested by computations; interesting but a local, finite-structure combinatorial conjecture.
latest_viability_rationale: Strong computational evidence up to r=7 and explicit local star/top capacity criteria plus staircase+one-cell candidate make a concrete, finite combinatorial proof plausible; remaining technical cases may still be nontrivial.
latest_label_rationale: Computations up to n≤30 support the triangular threshold formula, but the global statement is left explicitly as a conjecture and open problem.
latest_evidence_snippet: “The successive threshold gaps ... consistent with the triangular formula; these global statements are left as conjectures and open problems.” (local context lines 671-674, 686-685).

title: Simplex Stratification and Phase Boundaries in the Partition Graph
latest_interestingness_rationale: A clear combinatorial structural claim about first-occurrence layers tied to staircase partitions; supported computationally but confined to partition-graph theory, giving meaningful specialist content with limited broader impact.
latest_viability_rationale: Concrete local capacity criteria and exhaustive computations up to r=7 give a plausible concrete route; nontrivial global combinatorial work remains but resolution within 5 years is moderately likely.
latest_label_rationale: The paper presents this as an explicit conjecture supported by computations for n<=30 but does not prove it; authors state global statements remain conjectures and open problems.
latest_evidence_snippet: Computations suggest a rigid threshold pattern ... while the corresponding global statements are left as conjectures and open problems. (Conjecture: For every r≥2, L_r(τ(r)) consists exactly of partitions from δ_r with one added cell.)

title: Simplex Stratification and Phase Boundaries in the Partition Graph
latest_interestingness_rationale: A narrow, concrete characterization (L1 consists of the two antenna vertices) supported by data n≤30; valuable for the paper's stratification but mathematically local and technically specific.
latest_viability_rationale: Strong computational evidence (n≤30) and an exact local characterization via star/top capacities give a concrete combinatorial route to a proof; moderate near-term solvability, though sporadic large-n counterexamples remain possible.
latest_label_rationale: Authors observe data for 4≤n≤30 supporting the claim but explicitly state it as a conjecture and do not prove it in the paper.
latest_evidence_snippet: One particularly stable feature is |L_1(n)|=2 (4≤n≤30), these two vertices are (n),(1^n). The data further suggest that for all n≥4 the only vertices of local simplex dimension 1 are the two antenna vertices. (Conjecture stated.)

title: Simplex Stratification and Phase Boundaries in the Partition Graph
latest_interestingness_rationale: Structural claim that the framework lies in the two outermost layers, giving geometric insight into phase-boundaries; significant within this model but largely specialized to the partition-graph context.
latest_viability_rationale: Strong computational evidence (n≤30) and an exact local star/top capacity characterization reduce the problem to forbidding certain local configurations; plausible combinatorial closure but nontrivial to prove for all n—moderate short-term chance.
latest_label_rationale: The framework confinement statement is offered as a conjecture; computations support it but the authors explicitly note they do not have a proof.
latest_evidence_snippet: Taken together, these observations suggest that the framework remains confined to the low-simplex part of the graph. ... Conjecture: For every n≥4, Fw_n⊆L_1(n)∪L_2(n), Fw_n∩L_1(n)={ (n),(1^n) }.

title: Orbit-Level Stretching in Cubic Fourier-Galerkin Navier-Stokes: Sharp Incidence, Spectral Decay, and a Continuation Criterion
latest_interestingness_rationale: Asymptotic form of spherical incidence counts impacts lattice-point geometry and spectral estimates for Galerkin truncations; interesting within this geometric-analytic niche but limited in scope.
latest_viability_rationale: Depends on delicate lattice-point/cap-counting estimates (Bourgain–Rudnick style) for thin spherical shells; specialized but nontrivial. Partial techniques exist, so plausible but not imminent — moderate chance within five years.
latest_label_rationale: The spherical-incidence formula is stated as a conjectured expectation in the paper and is not proved; authors present it as an open question.
latest_evidence_snippet: Conjecture: “For the spherical truncation ... S^{sph}(N)=Θ(N^3 (log N)^c) for some c≥0.” (local context lines 2195-2201).

title: Orbit-Level Stretching in Cubic Fourier-Galerkin Navier-Stokes: Sharp Incidence, Spectral Decay, and a Continuation Criterion
latest_interestingness_rationale: A sign-cancellation exponent explaining extra spectral decay is relevant to orbit-level Navier–Stokes analysis and supported numerically, but is a narrowly focused, technically specialized conjecture.
latest_viability_rationale: Specific, quantified conjecture with strong numerics and a proven N^{-3/2} bound; likely solvable by spectral/random-matrix analysis quantifying skew-induced cancellations. Moderate uncertainty remains about technical challenges.
latest_label_rationale: The sign-cancellation exponent is posed explicitly as a conjecture with numerical evidence; no proof is given, so it remains open.
latest_evidence_snippet: Conjecture: “There exists δ>0 such that ... E[ρ(V_N)]=Θ(N^{-3/2-δ}). The numerical evidence suggests δ≈0.67.” (local context lines 2354-2366).

title: Counting points in thin sets: A survey
latest_label_rationale: The paper states Serre's projective thin-set conjecture has been largely resolved by recent work (BCSSV25x), so the exact conjecture as stated is no longer an open target.
latest_evidence_snippet: “Conjecture ... has now largely been resolved by the recent work of \cite{BCSSV25x}” (local context lines 334).

title: Counting points in thin sets: A survey
latest_interestingness_rationale: Serre/Heath-Brown Dimension Growth Conjecture is a central problem in rational-point counting; resolving it (and variants) has wide structural consequences for Diophantine geometry and thin-set asymptotics.
latest_viability_rationale: Survey states DGC (and uniform version) recently resolved in all but one case; remaining gap appears small and actively closed by recent breakthroughs, making near-term resolution likely.
latest_label_rationale: Authors report the Dimension Growth Conjecture was resolved in nearly all cases but not completely; the general statement remains unresolved as written.
latest_evidence_snippet: “We turn our attention to surveying works that recently resolved the Dimension Growth Conjecture ... in all but one case.” (local context lines 667-668).

title: Counting points in thin sets: A survey
latest_interestingness_rationale: The uniform DGC strengthens the main conjecture by removing extraneous dependence; proving uniformity would yield powerful, widely applicable bounds in arithmetic geometry and deepen understanding of coefficient-uniform phenomena.
latest_viability_rationale: Survey reports DGC and its uniform version resolved in all but one case via recent breakthroughs. A single remaining case suggests a concrete frontier, but its difficulty is unclear, so moderate–high near-term solvability is plausible.
latest_label_rationale: The paper states the Uniform Dimension Growth Conjecture is resolved in all but one case; the uniform version as stated therefore remains not fully settled.
latest_evidence_snippet: “... resolved the Dimension Growth Conjecture ..., as well as the Uniform Dimension Growth Conjecture ..., in all but one case.” (local context lines 667-668).

title: Counting points in thin sets: A survey
latest_interestingness_rationale: Uniform affine-hypersurface bounds are crucial for deducing projective results and much progress exists, but the statement is narrower (notably unresolved for cubics), making it a meaningful specialist conjecture.
latest_viability_rationale: Survey shows all homogeneous cases with d≠3 proved (recent breakthroughs); only homogeneous cubic case remains, with partial Salberger bounds. The gap is concrete and localized, but cubics are delicate—plausible but uncertain within 5 years.
latest_label_rationale: The authors and cited works prove the uniform affine hypersurface conjecture in many cases (all homogeneous d≠3), but they explicitly state the homogeneous degree d=3 uniform case remains open.
latest_evidence_snippet: “The Uniform Affine Dimension Growth Conjecture holds for homogeneous F with degree d ≠ 3... It remains an open problem ... for d=3.” (local context lines 863-869).

title: Counting points in thin sets: A survey
latest_interestingness_rationale: Serre's projective type II expectation addresses counting on type-II thin sets; it is central within the thin-set literature and has seen recent major advances, though some cases remain open.
latest_viability_rationale: Survey states BCSSV25x (2025) resolved the conjecture in nearly all cases; only limited remaining cases persist, so full resolution within five years is fairly likely.
latest_label_rationale: The paper records recent near-complete resolutions of the projective type II (Serre) conjecture but indicates it is resolved only 'in nearly all cases', so the full general conjecture remains open.
latest_evidence_snippet: “... the recent resolution of Conjecture \ref{conj_Serre_projII} by \cite{BCSSV25x} in nearly all cases...” (local context lines 1046).

title: Bohr's Last Problem Under the Entirety Hypothesis: A Survey with Initial Reductions
latest_interestingness_rationale: Analytic Lindel"of Hypothesis would impose strong structural constraints on order functions for entire Dirichlet series and has broad consequences (implies Lindel"of-type statements), making it highly significant across analytic number theory.
latest_viability_rationale: Deep analytic-number-theory refinement of Lindelöf; resolving ALH would likely require breakthroughs comparable to Lindelöf, so near-term resolution is unlikely.
latest_label_rationale: The Analytic Lindelöf Hypothesis (ALH) is introduced by the author as a central refinement and is not proved in the paper; it remains an open conjecture.
latest_evidence_snippet: Lines 171-176: "\begin{conjecture}[Analytic Lindel"of Hypothesis, ALH] Let L(s)=\sum a_n n^{-s} be ... Then μ(σ) is piecewise linear with slopes in Z_{\le0}. \end{conjecture}"

title: Bohr's Last Problem Under the Entirety Hypothesis: A Survey with Initial Reductions
latest_interestingness_rationale: A refined Sharp Kahane constraint controlling slopes where μ≥1; it sidesteps known obstructions and yields strong structural control relevant to Lindel"of-type deductions, significant within analytic theory of Dirichlet series.
latest_viability_rationale: A strong refined Sharp Kahane statement implying Lindelöf-type consequences; substantial arithmetic input seems necessary, making a five-year resolution improbable.
latest_label_rationale: The Refined Sharp Kahane conjecture is posed in the paper and not proved; it is presented as a stronger refinement and remains unresolved here.
latest_evidence_snippet: Lines 633-641: "\begin{conjecture}[Refined Sharp Kahane] Let L(s)=\sum a_n n^{-s} ... for all σ with μ(σ)≥1, μ(σ+μ(σ))=0. Equivalently: on any interval where μ≥1, the slope of μ is ≤-1. \end{conjecture}"

title: Bohr's Last Problem Under the Entirety Hypothesis: A Survey with Initial Reductions
latest_interestingness_rationale: A Cantor-weighted second-moment asymptotic for Hurwitz zeta that, if true, gives μ_L(1/2)=0 for the Cantor construction. Technically natural and impactful for this specific analytic route to Lindel"of.
latest_viability_rationale: A Cantor-weighted second-moment for Hurwitz zeta is plausible and numerically supported; still ties to difficult mean-square analysis, so conditional progress likely but unconditional proof uncertain.
latest_label_rationale: Conjecture H (Cantor-weighted Hurwitz α-second-moment) is stated as a conditional hypothesis that the authors do not prove; it is used to derive further consequences but remains open.
latest_evidence_snippet: Lines 1942-1949: "\begin{conjecture}[Cantor-weighted Hurwitz α-second-moment] ... \int |ζ(1/2+it,α)|^2 d\tildeν(α) = 1/2 log t + O(1) (t→∞). \end{conjecture}"

title: Bohr's Last Problem Under the Entirety Hypothesis: A Survey with Initial Reductions
latest_interestingness_rationale: A discrete-restriction inequality central to bounding an oscillatory term in the Cantor argument. Important for the paper's route but a narrow, technical analytic estimate with limited broader consequences.
latest_viability_rationale: A concrete discrete-restriction inequality with numerical evidence and a clear analytic target; may be approachable via harmonic-analysis techniques, giving moderate near-term feasibility.
latest_label_rationale: The Cantor-weighted discrete restriction conjecture is formulated in the paper as an open discrete-restriction inequality equivalent to bounding an oscillatory term; it is not proved here.
latest_evidence_snippet: Lines 2182-2191: "\begin{conjecture}[Cantor-weighted discrete restriction for the log-phase] ... \int |\sum_{n=1}^{M-1} n^{-1/2+it} e^{-inθ}|^2 d\tildeν(θ) ≤ C·H_{M-1}. \end{conjecture}"

title: Cambrian lattices are fractionally Calabi-Yau via 2-cluster combinatorics
body_tex:
Let $A=kL$ be the incidence algebra of a lattice $L$.
Then $A$ is combinatorially Serre formal if and only if $A$ is periodic Serre formal.
plain_text: Let $A=kL$ be the incidence algebra of a lattice $L$. Then $A$ is combinatorially Serre formal if and only if $A$ is periodic Serre formal.
latest_interestingness_rationale: Links combinatorial and periodic Serre-formality for incidence algebras of lattices. Valuable for classification in representation theory; important to specialists though technically focused and lattice-specific.

body_tex:
Let $D_k(n)$ be the diameter of $S_n$  Cayley graphs generated by consecutive cycles
                                                                     
of length $k$ and their inverses. They are given by quadratic quasi-polynomials in $n$ (for $n$ large enough) and the following holds:
\begin{enumerate}

    \item All the statements below  are valid for $ n \ge 2k. $ (The starting point for quasi-polynomials to be valid.)
                                                 

    \item The periods of  quasi-polynomials  are:
    \[
    \tau =
    \begin{cases}
    k - 1, & \text{if } k \text{ is even}, \\[4pt]
    2(k - 1), & \text{if } k \text{ is odd}.
    \end{cases}
    \]
    
                                                          
        
                             
        
        
    \item The general form of the diameter:
        
                                                           
        
    \[
    D_k(n) =  \frac{n(n-1)}{2(k-1)} + Q_0(n),
    \]    
    where $Q_0(n)$ is quasi-polynomial of degree zero, i.e. just the periodic function of $n$. 
    Moreover in many cases $Q_0(n)$ is just the correction to make the first term expression  to be the  integer 
                                   
    (floor/ceil), however it is not always the case.  

    
                                                          
    \item The last layer always contains either the full reversal
    $
    R = (n{-}1,\, n{-}2,\, \dots,\, 1,\, 0),
    $
    or its modified form with one adjacent inversion:
    $
    R' = R \circ (i,\, i{+}1).
    $
    
    \item The alternation between $R$ and $R'$ in the last layers has a period
    $
    T = k - 1.
    $ I.e.  the sequence $S(n) =$ $R$ or $R'$ whether the last layer contains $R$ or $R'$ will be periodic with the period $k-1$. 

                                                                               
    
    
\end{enumerate}

Moreover in many cases $Q_0(n)$ is just the correction to make the first term expression to be the integer (floor/ceil), however it is not always the case. The last layer always contains either the full reversal $ R = (n - 1,\, n - 2,\, ,\, 1,\, 0), $ or its modified form with one adjacent inversion: $ R' = R (i,\, i + 1). $ The alternation between $R$ and $R'$ in the last layers has a period $ T = k - 1. $ I.e. the sequence $S(n) =$ $R$ or $R'$ whether the last layer contains $R$ or $R'$ will be periodic with the period $k-1$.

Diameters of the Schreier coset graphs $S_n / ( S_{\lfloor n/2 \rfloor} \times S_{n-\lfloor n/2 \rfloor} )$
with consecutive $k$-cycles, not inverse closed case are given by :
\[
\begin{aligned}
n &\equiv 0 \!\pmod{(2k-2)} \;:& \!\!\!
D_k(n) &= \frac{n^2 + 4(k-1)}{4(k-1)}, \\[6pt]
n &\equiv -1 \!\pmod{(2k-2)} \;:& \!\!\!
D_k(n) &=  \frac{n^2 + 4(k-1)-1}{4(k-1)},
\end{aligned}
\]
and else, denoting $p = n \pmod{(2k-2)} $,
\[
\begin{aligned}
 D_k(n)= &  \frac{n(n+2k-p-2)}{4(k-1)}, & p  {\rm \ is \ even \ }
\\[6pt]
 D_k(n)= &   \frac{(n-1)(n+2k-p-2)}{4(k-1)}, & p  {\rm \ is \ odd \ }.
\end{aligned}
\]

body_tex:
(Not inverse closed case).
For consecutive $k$-cycle generators not inverse closed, the diameters of the 
Schreier coset graph: $S_n / \bigl(S_{l} \times S_{n-l}\bigr)$ (``$k$-shrunken''  Grassmannian $Gr(l,n,k)$)
are given by quasi-polynomials in two variables $n$ and $t = n-(l+1)$.

For $k=3$ with  period~$2$:
\[
D_l(n) = l\!\left(\left\lfloor \frac{t}{2} \right\rfloor + 1\right) + (t \bmod 2),
\qquad
t = n - (l+1), \quad n \ge l+1.
\]
Under the condition:  $l \ge 3$. For $l=2$, the formula is: 
$D_2(n) = n - 1, \qquad n \ge 4.$

For $k=4$ with  period~$3$ (again $t = n - (l+1)$):
\[
D_l(n) =
\begin{cases}
l, & t = 0, \\[2pt]
l+1, & t = 1, \\[2pt]
l+2, & t = 2, \\[6pt]
l\!\left( 2 + \left\lfloor \dfrac{t-3}{3} \right\rfloor \right),
& t \ge 3,\; t \equiv 0,1 \pmod{3}, \\[10pt]
l\!\left( 2 + \left\lfloor \dfrac{t-3}{3} \right\rfloor \right) + 1,
& t \ge 3,\; t \equiv 2 \pmod{3}.
\end{cases}
\]

For $k=5$ with  period~$4$ (again $t = n - (l+1)$,
for all $L \ge 4$, starting from
$ t+1 \ge 9 \qquad \text{that is,} \qquad N \ge L + 9$):
                                                                                      
\[
D(L,N) = L \left\lfloor \frac{t+1}{4} \right\rfloor + \mathbf{1}_{(t+1) \equiv 0 \; (\mathrm{mod}\ 4)} .
\]
plain_text: (Not inverse closed case). For consecutive $k$-cycle generators not inverse closed, the diameters of the Schreier coset graph: $S_n / (S_ l x S_ n-l )$ (``$k$-shrunken'' Grassmannian $Gr(l,n,k)$) are given by quasi-polynomials in two variables $n$ and $t = n-(l+1)$. For $k=3$ with period $2$: \[ D_l(n) = l\!( t 2 + 1) + (t 2), t = n - (l+1), n >= l+1. \] Under the condition: $l >= 3$. For $l=2$, the formula is: $D_2(n) = n - 1, n >= 4.$ For $k=4$ with period $3$ (again $t = n - (l+1)$): \[ D_l(n) = cases l, & t = 0, [2pt] l+1, & t = 1, [2pt] l+2, & t = 2, [6pt] l\!( 2 + t-3 3 ), & t >= 3,\; t 0,1 3, [10pt] l\!( 2 + t-3 3 ) + 1, & t >= 3,\; t 2 3. cases \] For $k=5$ with period $4$ (again $t = n - (l+1)$, for all $L >= 4$, starting from $ t+1 >= 9 that is, N >= L + 9$): \[ D(L,N) = L t+1 4 + 1_ (t+1) 0 \; (mod\ 4) . \]

title: The search for exotic knot traces
plain_text: Let $K$ be a knot with unknotting number one. Then the following are equivalent. $K$ is a twisted Whitehead double. For every unknotting crossing $x$ of $K$, the Piccirillo friends $K_x$ and $K'_x$ are isotopic to $K$. There exists an unknotting crossing $x$ of $K$ such that the Piccirillo friends $K_x$ and $K'_x$ are isotopic to $K$.

title: The GW/PT conjectures for toric pairs
body_tex:
\label{conj: gw/pt}
Fix a curve class $\beta$, partitions $\bm\mu$, and an insertion $\upalpha$.

    \begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item The PT series $Z_{\sf PT}(Y|\partial Y;q|\upalpha|\bm\mu)$ is the Laurent expansion of a rational function.
\item Under the change of variables $q = -e^{iu}$, there is an equality of generating functions:
\[
(-q)^{-d_\beta/2}\cdot Z_{\sf PT}(Y|\partial Y;q|\upalpha|\bm\mu)_\beta = (-iu)^{d_\beta+\sum \ell(\mu_j)-|\mu_j|} \cdot Z_{\sf GW}(Y|\partial Y;u|\upalpha|\bm\mu)_\beta.
\]
    \end{enumerate}
plain_text: Fix a curve class $$, partitions $$, and an insertion $$. [(i)] The PT series $Z_ PT (Y| Y;q||)$ is the Laurent expansion of a rational function. Under the change of variables $q = -e^ iu $, there is an equality of generating functions: \[ (-q)^ -d_/2 * Z_ PT (Y| Y;q||)_ = (-iu)^ d_+ ell (_j)-|_j| * Z_ GW (Y| Y;u||)_. \]
latest_interestingness_rationale: A deep GW/PT correspondence in the logarithmic (fully singular divisor) setting; solving it yields significant structural bridges in enumerative algebraic geometry and advances understanding of curve-counting theories.

title: Structure and Spectrum of Nonergodic Nilsystems
body_tex:
\label{Conj}
   Let $(X=G/\Gamma,\mu,T_1,\ldots,T_d)$ be an ergodic $\Z^d$-nilsystem. Then the Koopman representation of $(T_1,\ldots,T_d)$ on $L^2(X,\mu)$ decomposes as
    \[
L^2(X,\mu)=E_{\mathrm{ds}}\oplus E_{\mathrm{Leb}},
\]
where $E_{\mathrm{ds}}\cong L^2(G/G_2\Gamma)$ has discrete spectrum and $E_{\mathrm{Leb}}$, if nontrivial, splits into a countable orthogonal sum of invariant subspaces, each having maximal spectral type absolutely continuous with respect to the Haar measure of a nontrivial subtorus of $\bS^d$.

\label{conj:Mumford--Tate conjecture}
Fix a field embedding $K \subseteq \CC$. Let $\overline{K}$ be the algebraic closure of $K$ inside $\CC$. For any prime $\ell$, the isomorphism $\GL(\rH^{i}_{\et}(X_{\overline{K}},\QQ_{\ell})) \allowbreak\cong \GL(\rH^{i}_{B}(X))_{\QQ_{\ell}}$ via the Artin comparison isomorphism gives an identification
	\[
	\bG_{\ell,i}(X)^{\circ} =\MT_{i}(X_{\CC})_{\QQ_{\ell}}\,.
	\]
	Here $\bG_{\ell,i}(X)$ is the \emph{$\ell$-adic algebraic monodromy group} of $\rH^i_{\et}(X_{\overline{K}},\QQ_{\ell})$; and $\MT_i(X_{\CC})$ is the \emph{Mumford--Tate group} of the Hodge structure on the Betti cohomology $\rH^i_B(X,\QQ)$.

\[ \begin{matrix}

latest_viability_rationale: Paper claims the conjecture is resolved for all sufficiently large primes and prior work covers many ranges; only finitely many small primes remain, making full resolution likely within a few years.
latest_label_rationale: The paper proves the conjecture for large ranges of |S| and, combined with earlier work, for all sufficiently large primes p, but does not claim the full statement for every prime p; small primes may remain unresolved.
latest_evidence_snippet: Lines 61-62, 76-82: “Combined with earlier results, this gives a complete resolution of Graham's rearrangement conjecture for all sufficiently large primes p.” The conjecture as stated quantifies over any prime p.

title: Power monoids and their arithmetic: a survey

latest_viability_rationale: Specialized non-cancellative factorization problem with partial results but no clear finite reduction; active area but nontrivial and broad, so near-term full resolution seems uncertain.
latest_label_rationale: The statement is presented in the paper's 'Into the future' section as an open conjecture; the paper does not claim a proof and discusses partial progress.
latest_evidence_snippet: Lines 959-961: “If H is not a torsion monoid, then every non-empty subset ... can be realized as the length set of a set X ∈ P_{fin,1}(H).” (posed as a conjecture)

title: Power monoids and their arithmetic: a survey

plain_text: For each $l in N$, there exists an index $k in 0, l $ such that $_ 0, l <= <= _ k,l $ and $_ k,l >= >= _ l,l $.
latest_interestingness_rationale: Unimodality of atom-count sequences links combinatorial and arithmetic structure of power monoids; meaningful within factorization theory but relatively narrow and likely approachable by combinatorial/probabilistic methods.
latest_viability_rationale: New conjecture with experimental support and a partial result (holds for almost all l for H=ℕ). Non-classic, approachable combinatorial setting, but completing all l seems nontrivial.
latest_label_rationale: The paper states the Unimodality Conjecture as open; only partial progress is cited (holds for almost all l for H=N), so the exact statement remains unresolved.
latest_evidence_snippet: Lines 1071–1074: Conjecture stated. Lines 1082–1083: Aggarwal et al. show it holds for almost all l in the case H=ℕ (partial result).

title: Immersions with small normal curvature
body_tex:
\label{Conj:BiRic}
If $f: X^4\to \BB^N$ has $\fc(f) < \sqrt{\frac{12}{7}}$ then $g=f^*g_{\RR^N}$ is conformally equivalent to a metric of positive bi-Ricci curvature.
plain_text: If $f: X^4 to ^N$ has $(f) < 12 7 $ then $g=f^*g_ ^N $ is conformally equivalent to a metric of positive bi-Ricci curvature.
latest_interestingness_rationale: Connects an immersion curvature threshold to existence of positive bi-Ricci metrics in dimension four, with geometric and topological implications; central to curvature/immersion problems in the subfield.
latest_viability_rationale: Technical 4D geometric-analytic conjecture; authors obtain sphere-case and sharp constants but extension to general ball appears difficult and methodologically nontrivial.
latest_label_rationale: The BiRic conjecture is posed in the Remarks and Conjectures section and is not proved in the paper; only a special sphere-case is verified algebraically.
latest_evidence_snippet: Lines 808–811: Conjecture stated. Line 811: Holds if the immersion lies on the unit sphere S^{N-1}, but general case remains difficult.

title: Immersions with small normal curvature

For $X^n$ closed, if $f: X^n\to \BB^N$ has $\fc(f) < \sqrt{\frac 95}$ then $g=f^*g_{\RR^N}$ is conformally equivalent to a metric $\tilde g$ so that if $\tilde\lambda_1 \leq \dots \leq \tilde\lambda_4$ are the eigenvalues of $\widetilde\Ric$ at any point, then $\tilde \lambda_4 < \tilde\lambda_1+\tilde\lambda_2 + \tilde\lambda_3$.

latest_interestingness_rationale: Proposes a sharp eigenvalue inequality for conformally related Ricci tensors tied to immersion curvature bounds; technically significant for sharpness questions but narrower and more analytic.
latest_viability_rationale: Specific conformal-Ricci eigenvalue condition tied to geometric immersion bounds; plausible but requires new analytic tools beyond current partial/special-case arguments.
latest_label_rationale: The imo-ric conjecture is explicitly proposed and not proved; the authors pose it as an open problem and ask whether S^2×T^2 admits such a metric.
latest_evidence_snippet: Lines 814–816: Conjecture stated. Line 817: Authors note it is an interesting (open) problem to determine if S^2×T^2 admits such a metric.

title: Fano varieties with split tangent sheaf
latest_interestingness_rationale: Beauville's conjecture is a longstanding, central problem: integrable tangent splitting implies universal‑cover product decomposition, with wide consequences across complex/Kähler geometry and manifold structure theory.
latest_viability_rationale: Longstanding (Beauville 1998) conjecture with substantial partial progress (projective/Fano cases, integrability results). Active research but full compact Kähler statement remains unresolved; modest chance of full resolution in five years.
latest_label_rationale: Beauville's conjecture is stated as a well-known open problem; the paper proves special (Fano/mildly singular) cases but does not resolve the conjecture in full generality.

title: Fano varieties with split tangent sheaf

latest_viability_rationale: Active field with substantial partial results and concrete MMP/induction strategy; remaining global integrability steps nontrivial but plausibly closable within a few years.

latest_viability_rationale: Active research and explicit ideas (Shende) plus connections to wild nonabelian Hodge/P=W, but several nontrivial steps remain; full retract and weight-to-perverse statement uncertain within five years.

title: Pruning distance of upset-decomposable persistence modules
latest_interestingness_rationale: Asserts Lipschitz equivalence between pruning and interleaving distances—central to stability and metric comparisons in persistence theory, with clear structural and practical consequences if resolved.
latest_viability_rationale: Active area with partial results (including this paper's sharp bound for upset-decomposable modules); full general Lipschitz equivalence to interleaving distance remains nontrivial but plausibly resolved in coming years.
latest_label_rationale: The conjecture (d_P ≤ d_I ≤ 2r d_P for pfd modules) is stated and discussed as open; this paper proves related results for upset-decomposable modules but not the full general statement.

title: Irreducible distinguishing colourings and the Axiom of Choice
body_tex:
The following statements are equivalent the Axiom of Choice in ZF assuming the definition of a cardinal number as  an equivalence class of the equinumerous relation.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textnormal{\arabic*)}]
    \item Every infinite connected graph has a chromatic index.
    \item Every infinite connected graph has a distinguishing chromatic number.
    \item Every infinite connected graph has a distinguishing chromatic index.
    \item Every infinite connected graph has a distinguishing number.
    \item Every infinite connected graph has a distinguishing chromatic index.
\end{enumerate}
plain_text: The following statements are equivalent the Axiom of Choice in ZF assuming the definition of a cardinal number as an equivalence class of the equinumerous relation. [label=)] Every infinite connected graph has a chromatic index. Every infinite connected graph has a distinguishing chromatic number. Every infinite connected graph has a distinguishing chromatic index. Every infinite connected graph has a distinguishing number. Every infinite connected graph has a distinguishing chromatic index.
latest_interestingness_rationale: Proposes equivalence of natural infinite-graph colouring/existence statements to the Axiom of Choice; a resolution would have broad foundational consequences linking combinatorics and set theory.
latest_viability_rationale: Equivalences to the Axiom of Choice are classic set-theoretic questions; resolution likely requires model/independence techniques—feasible but may be delicate, giving modest near-term solvability odds.
latest_label_rationale: Authors explicitly mark the question as still open and state the equivalence-to-Choice list as a conjecture; no proof within the paper.
latest_evidence_snippet: Lines 127–136: 'Furthermore, the question mentioned below is still open to the best of our knowledge. Conj: The following statements are equivalent [to AC in ZF]: (1) Every infinite connected graph has a chromatic index; ... (5) Every infinite connected graph has a distinguishing chromatic index.'

title: A new problem related to Eulerian graphs
body_tex: Let $k$ be a natural number. The problem of determining whether a given subgraph $H$ with at most $k$ components of a finite graph $G$ is $S$-Eulerian (semi $S$-Eulerian) is polynomial in time.
plain_text: Let $k$ be a natural number. The problem of determining whether a given subgraph $H$ with at most $k$ components of a finite graph $G$ is $S$-Eulerian (semi $S$-Eulerian) is polynomial in time.
latest_interestingness_rationale: Natural fixed-k extension of the connected-case algorithmic result; useful for complexity classification but limited conceptual novelty or wider mathematical consequences beyond this specific problem.
latest_viability_rationale: For fixed k, parameterized/DP or enumeration often yields polynomial algorithms. Paper proves k=1 linear and NP-complete in general, so bounded-component polynomiality is plausible and likely reachable within five years.
latest_label_rationale: The author explicitly poses this as a conjecture (Section Introduction) and the paper does not prove or refute it; only special cases (connected H) and hardness for general H are proved.
latest_evidence_snippet: Lines 64-68: 'Further research ... we propose the following conjecture. Let k be a natural number. The problem ... with at most k components ... is polynomial in time.'

\label{conj:any-solvable-tower-core}

title: Mock modularity of log Gromov--Witten Invariants: the mirror to $\mathbb{P}^2$
body_tex:
Let $\phi: Y \to B$ be an elliptic fibration and $D\subset Y$ a normal crossing divisor such that $\phi(D)$ is a divisor in $B$. Assume that the generic fiber of the restricted morphism $\phi|_{D} \colon D \to \phi(D)$ is either a cycle of $\PP^1$'s or a nodal elliptic curve. Then the generating series of logarithmic Gromov–Witten invariants of $(Y,D)$, 
\[ \sum_{d \geq 0} GW^{(Y,D)}_{g,v,\beta_0+dF} q^d \,, \]
where $v$ is a fixed contact order along $D$, $\beta_0 \in H_2(Y,\ZZ)$ is a fixed curve class, and $F$ denotes the fiber class, is a component of a (higher depth) vector-valued mock modular form, up to appropriate normalization in the power of $q$.

\]

\label{conj:AT-IGMC} Let $D\subset\mathbb C$ be a Jordan domain with discrete domain approximation $D_\de\subset\delta\Z^2$. At each point of the critical line~\eqref{eq:critical}, as $\de\to0$, 
	the nesting field of the AT current on $D_\de$ under the $+/+$ or free/free boundary conditions converges to 
	\[
	\frac{1}{2\lambda\sqrt{g}}\ \GFF = \frac{1}{\pi\sqrt{g}}\ \GFF,
	\] 
	where $\GFF$ is a GFF with zero boundary conditions in $D$, and $g$ is defined in~\eqref{eq:defg}. 
	Moreover, the polarisation fields under $+/+$ and free/free boundary conditions, respectively, converge to
		\[
			\cos\big(h/\sqrt{g}\big) \quad \text{and} \quad	\sin \big(h/\sqrt{g}\big),
		\]
	corresponding to the \emph{imaginary Gaussian multiplicative chaos} with parameter $\alpha(g)=1/\sqrt{g}\in[1/2, \sqrt{3}/2)\subset[0, \sqrt{2}].$

title: The Ising magnetisation field and the Gaussian free field
body_tex:
\label{conj:AT-inter}
	Consider the clusters of the decomposition described in Conjecture \ref{conj:AT-IGMC} under $+/+$ boundary conditions. Toss a fair coin for each cluster to assign a value $+1$ or $-1$, except for the boundary cluster which is assigned $+1$. If two clusters with the value $+1$ (resp. $-1$) touch each other, we say that they belong to the same $\oplus$-cluster (resp. $\ominus$-cluster). Then, the law of the outermost interfaces of the Ashkin-Teller magnetisation field is given by the outermost outer boundaries of the $\ominus$-clusters. The full collection of interfaces is defined iteratively.
plain_text: Consider the clusters of the decomposition described in Conjecture under $+/+$ boundary conditions. Toss a fair coin for each cluster to assign a value $+1$ or $-1$, except for the boundary cluster which is assigned $+1$. If two clusters with the value $+1$ (resp. $-1$) touch each other, we say that they belong to the same $$-cluster (resp. $$-cluster). Then, the law of the outermost interfaces of the Ashkin-Teller magnetisation field is given by the outermost outer boundaries of the $$-clusters. The full collection of interfaces is defined iteratively.
latest_interestingness_rationale: Describes a natural continuum percolation construction of AT interfaces via coin-flipped cluster signs; interesting structural picture but narrower and conditional on earlier conjectures.
latest_viability_rationale: More geometric and iterative, relying on earlier conjectures; plausible conditional on those but more speculative and technically delicate, lowering near-term solvability.
latest_label_rationale: The continuum percolation description of AT interfaces is stated as Conjecture~\ref{conj:AT-inter} and is not proved in the paper.

title: Dead ends in square-free digit walks
comments: After we posted the first version on arXiv, we learned from K. Soundararajan that the result in this paper was previously obtained by Mirsky in 1947. We mistakenly assumed that the 2024 paper of Miller et al. represented the status of this problem. Their paper makes no reference to Mirsky; his work seems to have been forgotten. This manuscript will not be submitted for journal publication

title: On the Graphical $r$-Stirling Numbers of the First Kind for Specific Graph Families
body_tex:
\label{conj:unimodal-planar}
For any planar graph $G$ of order $n$, the sequence of graphical Stirling numbers
\[
\{\st{G}{k}\}_{k=1}^n
\]
is \emph{unimodal}, i.e., there exists an index $k_0$ such that
\[
\st{G}{1} \le \cdots \le \st{G}{k_0} \ge \cdots \ge \st{G}{n}.
\]
This property is known for paths, cycles, trees, lollipop, and Tadpole graphs.
